BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.

- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / internal. Seller documents treated as the counterparty's draft, reviewed against the Buyer Playbook only.

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. Measured against our playbook, the Seller Update departs on **every** liability and protection item, and in several places it goes further than a conventional seller-favourable opening by trying to collapse the fundamental, fraud, tax and IP regimes into the general cap. Several of the Seller's SPA assertions are also **contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter** (Bluefen consent "addressed" vs "NOT included"; Riverlark "addressed" vs "NOT repaid"; title "evidenced" vs "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification"). Those internal inconsistencies are useful leverage.

Nothing in this draft can be accepted on the fallback positions. The 20% cap and 18-month period are conditional fallbacks that require prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this specific draft; **no such authority exists**, so we respond at our starting positions (25% / AUD 6,000,000; 24 months).

One further point: the Disclosure Letter is cut off at **22 September 2026**. Today is 6 November 2026 – six weeks have passed. Before any further mark-up we should require a bring-down update on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the DD-006 incident and the Sandbar renewals, as the positions stated may no longer be current.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. General Warranty cap (Clause 12.1)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | Start 25% / AUD 6,000,000; 20% is a fallback only with Amelia Frost's written sign-off on this draft | **Reject.** No authority given. The Seller's figure happens to match our fallback, which is a reason to be careful: conceding it now spends our only fallback at the first exchange and leaves nothing for later trades on time limits or thresholds. |

**Push back:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. If the team wants to use the fallback, obtain Amelia Frost's written authority first, expressly identifying "Seller Update draft (SPA-003)".

### B. Thresholds (Clause 12.2)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded | **Reject on all three limbs.** The de minimis is 5x ours and the basket is 5x ours, and the excess-only (deductible) structure converts the basket into a hard AUD 250,000 loss we bear on every deal outcome. Against a AUD 24m price, a AUD 250,000 deductible plus a AUD 25,000 per-claim floor would exclude most realistic warranty claims in a business of this size (the Ironquay exposure of AUD 180,000, for example, would be barely over the basket). |

**Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket (first dollar). No deductible.

### C. Time limits and the "applies to all Claims" override (Clause 12.3 / 13)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| 18 months; "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | 24 months; 18 is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval (none given); keep categories separate, no hidden general-regime override | **Reject.** 18 months is outside authority. The second sentence is the more dangerous one: it is a **default-in** rule that would sweep fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims into the 18-month window and the 20% cap unless we remember to carve each one out. The drafting burden is reversed. |

**Push back:** 24 months for general claims; delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence and replace with the reverse: limitations in Clause 12 apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title Warranties, Tax, IP (if agreed separately), payment obligations, covenants or specific indemnities.

### D. Fundamental / Title warranties

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | **Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title or capacity fails we have not bought the company; a AUD 4.8m cap on a AUD 24m purchase of non-existent shares is not a commercial outcome. This is a non-negotiable for the Buyer. |

**Push back:** Separate Fundamental Warranty regime: cap = purchase price; period = 6 years minimum; expressly outside Clause 12.2 thresholds, Clause 8.3 knowledge bar and Schedule 7 disclosure.

### E. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| All limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to every Claim without exception | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this | **Reject.** The draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**. Read with the Clause 13 "all Claims" override, the Seller's position is that fraudulent misrepresentation is capped at AUD 4.8m, time-barred after 18 months, subject to the basket, and excluded by non-reliance. Quite apart from being commercially unacceptable, a clause purporting to exclude liability for fraud is of doubtful enforceability under NSW law, which means the Seller is seeking an advantage it likely cannot keep while shifting litigation risk to us. This item is a red line; the playbook says no one on our side can waive it. |

**Push back:** Insert an express carve-out: nothing in the Agreement limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, the Company or any of their officers/advisers, and the non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clauses do not apply to such matters.

### F. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| General disclosure of the entire indexed data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure | **Reject.** §1.1 and §1.2 are classic whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure. Combined with Clause 8.3 it means every document in the room is treated as disclosed against every warranty regardless of whether it fairly alerts the Buyer to the issue. §1.4 ("nothing admits breach… or that any consent… is legally required") also means the Seller is disclosing the existence of documents while expressly declining to disclose their legal consequence – the opposite of fair disclosure. |

**Push back:** Replace §1.1–1.2 with a specific disclosure standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect. Delete public-register deemed disclosure. We should also respond to §1.4 by stating that the Buyer does not accept the Seller's characterisations and reserves all rights.

### G. Buyer knowledge exclusion (Clause 8.3)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| No claim for any matter the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" | Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier must be by named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity | **Reject.** This is a blanket exclusion with three aggravating features: (i) imputed knowledge of advisers; (ii) "discoverable" – i.e., constructive knowledge, not actual; (iii) tied to the whole data room and public records, which doubles down on the deemed-disclosure point. In practice it would make the warranties almost unenforceable: the Seller would argue every matter was "discoverable" somewhere in DD-002 to DD-012. |

**Push back:** Delete Clause 8.3. If the Seller insists on any knowledge concept, it must be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals, and must expressly not apply to Fundamental/Title Warranties, fraud or any specific indemnity. Our preferred position remains deletion.

### H. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| "Addressed"; Seller to use reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent | Require effective consent **and** evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer | **Reject – and note the contradiction.** The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (§2) confirms Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue, that consent under clause 11.2 is conditional on 11.3, and that **no final written consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction** has been provided. "Addressed" in the SPA Update is therefore inaccurate. A consent-on-delivery mechanic means a consent subject to unsatisfied conditions (e.g. pricing changes, guarantees, or a termination right) would be treated as satisfied. Losing 30% of revenue post-Completion is a price-level issue. |

**Push back:** Bluefen is a Condition Precedent. Satisfaction requires (a) unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 in a form approved by the Buyer, and (b) evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied or waived by Bluefen, both before Completion. Replace "reasonable endeavours" with "all reasonable endeavours" plus a positive obligation to procure. Consider a price adjustment or specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or re-prices within an agreed period after Completion.

### I. Riverlark facility (Clauses 2 / 7)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" | Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; a post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval | **Reject.** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release means we pay AUD 24m for a company that still carries AUD 3.2m of secured bank debt and whose assets remain subject to Riverlark's security at the moment we take ownership. Disclosure Letter §3 confirms nothing has been repaid and no discharge exists. Change-of-control clause 8.1 also means Completion itself may trigger an event of default unless Riverlark has consented. No Amelia Frost approval exists for a post-Completion release. |

**Push back:** Require (a) a payout letter from Riverlark current as at Completion; (b) repayment directly from Completion funds via the funds flow, with the price reduced accordingly; (c) executed deeds of release / PPSR discharges delivered at Completion; and (d) Riverlark's confirmation that cl 8.1 change-of-control will not be triggered or is waived. If the Seller cannot deliver releases at Completion, the fallback requires an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark *and* Amelia Frost's written approval – not to be offered without both.

### J. Funds flow and employee bonuses (DD-005)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Bonuses of AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller", not itemised | Must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them; on-costs must be included | **Reject.** Disclosure Letter §5 confirms the AUD 420,000 is conditional on Completion and continued employment, and is **not** in the funds flow, and is silent on superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs. If these are paid by the Company post-Completion, Wattlebridge funds them. The Seller saying it is "a matter for the Seller" is not a drafting mechanism – it needs to be either a price deduction or a Seller payment obligation. On-costs are a genuine incremental exposure (superannuation and payroll tax on a AUD 420,000 bonus pool could be a material add-on). |

**Push back:** Add a specific line item: AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, leave accruals if applicable) either (a) deducted from the purchase price as a Transaction Cost / Debt-like item, or (b) paid by the Seller to the Company immediately before Completion with evidence. Seek a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Request the Seller quantify on-costs.

### K. Ironquay IP indemnity (Clause 11.1)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" | Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way | **Reject as drafted.** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. So the Company may not currently own IP it is using. The Seller's indemnity covers only the payment – not loss of use, infringement claims, re-development cost, customer claims or the cost of obtaining a confirmatory assignment. We should not assume AUD 180,000 is the right figure; DD-010 is an internal ledger entry, not bank verification. |

**Push back:** (a) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure either evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees or a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, and a current statement of account; (b) indemnity broadened to all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to hold good title to the SOW3 Project Materials or any Ironquay-originated IP, including infringement, remediation and replacement costs, outside the general cap and basket; (c) preserve the cure mechanic – payment of the outstanding fees is a permitted route to cure, with the indemnity covering the cost.

### L. DD-006 export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction | **Do not accept the characterisation, but do not overstate it either.** The Disclosure Letter is actually more careful than the SPA Update: ~1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; notification question open. Six weeks have now passed since the disclosure date. We should neither accept "not material" nor assert that a notifiable breach has occurred. |

**Push back:** (a) Require a written investigation update to a date within 5 business days of signing, and again at Completion; (b) Seller covenant to preserve all logs, link-access records and correspondence and to give the Buyer access; (c) a warranty that the Seller has disclosed all information known about the incident; (d) a specific indemnity for Loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification, customer claims) outside the general cap, drafted neutrally so it does not pre-judge whether a breach occurred; (e) a right to require the Seller to cooperate on any notification decision pre-Completion. We should not put a number on this.

### M. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | **Hold – do not concede, do not demand a deduction yet.** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The Disclosure Letter candidly says it does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – which is exactly the information we need. Read together, if they commit the Company for a new term post-Completion they may be a pre-Completion liability or a locked-box leakage issue; if they are genuine recurring opex they are not. |

**Push back:** Request (a) the renewal terms, notice periods and commencement dates; (b) confirmation of whether any has been signed or accrued as at the locked-box / Completion accounts date; (c) an undertaking that no further renewal is entered into without Buyer consent pre-Completion. Decide on classification after assessment.

### N. Tax / IP warranties

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | **Reject the "settled" characterisation.** Nothing has been agreed. Folding tax and IP into the 20% / 18-month / basket regime is a substantive concession dressed as housekeeping. Tax exposures typically require longer periods (tied to statutory amendment windows) and a tax indemnity; IP goes to the core of an analytics business. |

**Push back:** State expressly that Tax and IP are open items to be negotiated separately with their own cap and time period and are excluded from the Clause 13 override. Do not propose unlimited liability; do not propose figures until the team has settled a position.

### O. Title evidence (DD-012)

| Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012" | Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal source, not independent proof | **Reject as sufficient.** Disclosure Letter §10 itself concedes that DD-012 merely "identifies the source relied on" and does not confirm Buyer verification. A share register is prepared by the Company and can be wrong or incomplete (e.g., unregistered transfers, options, security interests over shares). |

**Push back:** Require (a) current ASIC company extract; (b) PPSR search over Harbourglass and the Company for security interests over shares and assets (noting Riverlark's security will appear); (c) original share certificates or confirmation of none issued; (d) Seller board resolutions and constitutional authority to sell; (e) warranty that there are no options, rights or encumbrances over the shares, backed by the Fundamental regime in D above.

### P. Other disclosure items (lease, Mossvale)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Disclosure says notification only, not consent. Request the clause and confirm. Covenant for the Seller to give the notification pre-Completion with evidence.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Restriction on assignment; Seller says no consent needed for a share sale. Request the clause; confirm there is no change-of-control trigger (assignment restrictions are often paired with one). Low priority if confirmed.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Red lines – do not move:**
1. Insert a full fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. No one on our side has authority to waive this.
2. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, 6+ years, outside thresholds, knowledge bar and disclosure.
3. Delete the Clause 13 "all Claims" override; replace with an express statement that general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
4. Delete Clause 8.3 (buyer knowledge) in its entirety.
5. Replace whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure with specific fair disclosure.

**Starting positions – counter, no fallback authority exists:**
6. Cap: 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (not 20%).
7. Time limit: 24 months (not 18).
8. Thresholds: AUD 5,000 de minimis / AUD 50,000 tipping basket, first-dollar recovery.
9. Tax and IP: expressly open; separate regime to follow.

**Completion mechanics – fix before signing:**
10. Bluefen: unconditional consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a CP; "all reasonable endeavours" plus procure obligation; consider price protection.
11. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases and PPSR discharges at Completion, cl 8.1 waiver. Post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost written approval.
12. Bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, with indemnity; ask Seller to quantify on-costs.
13. Title: independent evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR, certificates, authority) – DD-012 alone is insufficient.

**Specific risk items:**
14. Ironquay: pre-Completion payment evidence or confirmatory assignment; broadened indemnity outside the cap; SOW3 cure preserved; treat AUD 180,000 as unverified.
15. DD-006: log preservation covenant, investigation updates, neutral specific indemnity; no number, no characterisation either way.
16. Sandbar: information request; no classification or deduction until assessed.

**Process:**
17. Require a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter to a current date – the 22 September 2026 cut-off is six weeks stale.
18. Use the Seller's internal inconsistencies (SPA Update "addressed/evidenced/settled" vs Disclosure Letter "not included/not repaid/not verified/open") in the cover response.
19. If the team wishes to deploy either fallback (20% cap or 18 months), obtain Amelia Frost's written authority first, expressly identifying this draft (SPA-003 Seller Update). None exists today.

I can prepare the mark-up of Clauses 8.3, 9.3, 11.1, 12, 13 and 20.5 and a draft response to the Disclosure Letter on this basis if useful.
